title: Farah Khan Just Locked 15 Celebrities in a Prison — and Govinda's Wife Isn't Even the Wildest Part
excerpt: Lock Upp Season 2 exploded onto Netflix this weekend with a divorce bombshell, a bloody on-set injury, and Urfi Javed making an entrance nobody asked for but everyone watched.
body:
The first episode hadn't even ended, and the internet was already on fire.

Lock Upp: Sach Ya Sazaa — the reality show that made Kangana Ranaut a jailer before she became a politician — is back. Season 2 premiered on Netflix on Friday, June 27, and within hours, it had already delivered more drama than most scripted series manage in an entire season. The show has traded MX Player for Netflix, Kangana for Farah Khan and Riteish Deshmukh, and restraint for absolute chaos. It's louder, messier, and more watchable than it has any right to be.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=i8UyGe67fys

The setup remains deliciously cruel: 15 celebrity contestants are locked inside a prison-themed set for six weeks, forced to survive tasks, chargesheets, eliminations, and — worst of all — each other. Ekta Kapoor produces. New episodes stream Saturday through Wednesday at 8 PM IST. And if the first 48 hours are any indication, this season is going to leave marks.

![Lock Upp — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/2/20/Lock_Upp_logo.jpg)

The Lineup Is Stacked

Forget the usual Instagram influencer filler. This cast has weight. Ram Kapoor — the man who built a career on being the most comfortable person in every room — walked in with the kind of energy that suggests he's here to win or, at minimum, to make everyone else deeply uncomfortable. Shivangi Joshi of *Yeh Rishta Kya Kehlata Hai* fame brings a massive television fanbase. Dheeraj Dhoopar, known to fans as the "Shah Rukh Khan of television," tried to make a dramatic entrance by pretending to escape, because apparently no one told him that subtlety is an option.

> "Dheeraj Dhoopar, known to fans as the "Shah Rukh Khan of television," tried to make a dramatic entrance by pretending to escape, because apparently no one told him that subtlety is an option."

Then there's Sunita Ahuja — Govinda's wife, a woman who has spent decades in Bollywood's orbit without ever quite being in Bollywood. She's candid, she's opinionated, and she's already generating the kind of quotes that PR teams have nightmares about. Harshad Chopda (*Bepannah*, *Left Right Left*) brings legitimate acting chops to a format that rarely rewards them. Riyaz Aly, the social media star with 30 million followers, represents the generation that doesn't remember a world before reels. And rounding out the chaos: content creators Shreya Kalra and Sufi Motiwala, reality veteran Yogesh Rawat, and Shreshta Iyer — yes, cricketer Shreyas Iyer's sister.

The Bombshell That Detonated on Night One

![Kangana Ranaut — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f4/Kangana_Ranaut_at_Ira_Khan%27s_wedding_reception_%28cropped%29.jpg)

The headline out of the premiere isn't about tasks or alliances — it's about a marriage ending on national television. Akanksha Chamola, best known as the wife of *Anupamaa* star Gaurav Khanna, confirmed during her introduction that the couple is heading for a divorce after nearly a decade together. They've been living separately for a year, she said. The decision was mutual. There's no bitterness.

The internet, predictably, had opinions. An old *Bigg Boss* clip of Gaurav resurfaced within hours — one where he mentioned Akanksha not being ready to have children — and speculation about whether differing views on family contributed to the split spread like wildfire. Rakhi Sawant weighed in from the comments section, calling Akanksha a liar with a laughing emoji, because of course she did.

The Hosts Are the Show's Secret Weapon

Farah Khan and Riteish Deshmukh are, on paper, an unusual pairing. In practice, they're magnetic. Farah brings the authority — she's been directing rooms full of the biggest egos in Bollywood for two decades — and Riteish brings the mischief. His stated strategy: ruin every contestant's game plan before they even know they had one. Together, they have a warmth that Kangana's season never quite achieved, making the cruelty of the format feel like it comes from a place of entertainment rather than judgment.

![Riteish Deshmukh — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/eb/Riteish_Deshmukh_at_the_Promotion_of_%27Kyaa_Super_Kool_Hain_Hum%27_06.jpg)

> "Everyone will have to wash their own clothes here." — Farah Khan, establishing dominance on day one

Already Drawing Blood — Literally

By day one, things had already turned physical. During an early task, Harshad Chopda accidentally injured Sunita Ahuja, an incident that immediately became the most-discussed moment on social media after the divorce reveal. Details remain sketchy — the show is clearly saving the full footage for maximum impact — but the fact that it happened within 24 hours tells you everything about the intensity of this season's energy.

Where to Watch

Lock Upp Season 2 streams exclusively on Netflix, making it one of the most accessible Indian reality shows for the diaspora. New episodes drop Saturday through Wednesday at 8 PM IST (10:30 AM ET / 7:30 AM PT). The six-week run means a finale sometime in early August.

For NRI audiences who grew up on *Bigg Boss* but have grown tired of its bloated 100-episode seasons, Lock Upp's tight six-week format and Netflix accessibility make it the obvious alternative. It's fast, it's messy, and it knows exactly what it is.

The prison doors are locked. The cameras are rolling. And somebody's marriage just ended on the first night. Welcome to the most entertaining disaster on Indian television.
